newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes down in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes down in moderate trade.

text.p: Rubber futures slipped at the close on Tuesday in moderate trade on the back of weak sentiment and soft prices in Tokyo's rubber market, dealers said.

Most of the buying was concentrated in spot RSS3 February contract, with the amount traded reaching nearly 1,400 tonnes, traders said. The next most active month was the TSR20 February contract with about 900 tonnes traded.
"Some people took advantage of the low prices to lock in their supplies," a dealer for a Western trading house said.
"We saw some buying by local dealers who saw a good bargain in the low prices in the market," a rubber dealer said.
A slight fall in Tokyo's benchmark June contract, which slipped 1.9 yen to settle at 146.8, encouraged local players to mark their prices lower, one dealer said.

"When Tokyo went down, sentiment here became really soft," one dealer said. At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 122.50-124.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 124.50 cents. March RSS1 was at 176.00-178.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from the previous 178.75 cents.
March TSR20 was at 169.50-171.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg from 171.50 cents.
